question:
A 73-year-old man comes to the physician because of progressive fatigue and shortness of breath on exertion for 3 weeks. He has swelling of his legs. He has not had nausea or vomiting. His symptoms began shortly after he returned from a trip to Cambodia. He occasionally takes ibuprofen for chronic back pain. He has a history of arterial hypertension and osteoarthritis of both knees. He had an episode of pneumonia 4 months ago. His current medications include lisinopril and hydrochlorothiazide. He has no history of drinking or smoking. His temperature is 37°C (98.6°F), pulse is 101/min, and blood pressure is 135/76 mm Hg. Examination shows pitting edema of the upper and lower extremities. Laboratory studies show:
Hemoglobin 14.1 g/dL
Leukocyte count 6,800/mm3
Platelet count 216,000/mm3
Serum
Urea nitrogen 26 mg/dL
Creatinine 2.9 mg/dL
Albumin 1.6 g/L
Urine
Blood negative
Protein 4+
Glucose negative
Renal biopsy with Congo red stain shows apple-green birefringence under polarized light. Further evaluation of this patient is most likely to show which of the following findings?"?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "73-year-old man with progressive fatigue" -> "possible underlying systemic condition" -> "recent travel to Cambodia" -> "risk for infectious or tropical diseases" -> "renal biopsy shows apple-green birefringence" -> "indicative of amyloidosis" -> "common in chronic inflammatory conditions" -> "possible rouleaux formation due to increased proteins" -> 85%

CHAIN: "73-year-old man with pitting edema" -> "suggests fluid overload or renal issue" -> "elevated creatinine indicates renal impairment" -> "renal biopsy shows apple-green birefringence" -> "consistent with amyloidosis" -> "amyloidosis can cause increased serum proteins" -> "may lead to rouleaux formation on peripheral smear" -> 80%

CHAIN: "73-year-old man with shortness of breath" -> "possible heart failure or pulmonary issue" -> "edema suggests fluid retention" -> "renal biopsy shows apple-green birefringence" -> "indicates amyloidosis" -> "amyloidosis can affect multiple organ systems" -> "may not directly correlate with HLA-B27 or anti-citrullinated antibodies" -> 70%

CHAIN: "73-year-old man with chronic back pain" -> "takes ibuprofen" -> "possible chronic inflammation" -> "renal biopsy shows apple-green birefringence" -> "indicative of amyloidosis" -> "amyloidosis can be associated with chronic inflammatory states" -> "but not specifically linked to elevated anti-citrullinated peptide antibodies" -> 75%

CHAIN: "73-year-old man with recent pneumonia" -> "possible chronic infection or inflammation" -> "renal biopsy shows apple-green birefringence" -> "consistent with amyloidosis" -> "amyloidosis can be secondary to chronic infections" -> "but does not correlate with positive interferon-γ release assay" -> 65%
analysis: The patient's symptoms and laboratory findings suggest a diagnosis of amyloidosis, particularly given the renal involvement indicated by proteinuria and the renal biopsy showing apple-green birefringence with Congo red staining. In cases of amyloidosis, especially AL amyloidosis, one would expect to see rouleaux formation on peripheral smear due to increased serum proteins. The other options do not correlate with the findings or the likely diagnosis.
